modules.title: Orientation & Electrical Safety
objectives: Explain how current affects the human body and why 'low voltage' can still hurt you or the hardware
Apply lockout/tagout, PPE and safe bench practices
Recognize fire classes and extinguisher types; respond to a shock incident
topics: Shock physiology, arc flash awareness (NFPA 70E concepts)
LOTO, PPE, bench & tool safety, battery/stored-energy hazards (capacitors)
labs: LOTO practical on a training panel
modules.assessment: Written safety quiz (100% required, may retake); LOTO practical sign-off
modules.notes: Safety tops CETa, Nida, Navy and USAF syllabi. Add site EHS rules.

modules.title: ESD Control & Part Handling
objectives: Describe how ESD damages parts, including latent damage
Correctly use wrist straps, mats, smocks, ionizers and ESD packaging
Verify personal grounding before work
topics: Wrist-strap/footwear testers, packaging, moisture-sensitive device awareness
labs: Field-meter demo of charge generation by common materials
modules.assessment: Quiz (80%); daily wrist-strap check log
modules.notes: Aerospace: ANSI/ESD S20.20 site control plan (required by NASA-STD-8739.6).

modules.title: Technician Math & Units
objectives: Use SI prefixes, scientific & engineering notation fluently
Rearrange simple formulas; use ratios, percentages and tolerances
Use basic trig/vectors needed for AC; read binary/hex
topics: Metric prefixes (p, n, µ, m, k, M, G)
labs: Calculator drills; converting meter readings between units
Tolerance worksheet using real resistor values
modules.assessment: Written test (80%)
modules.notes: Kept short and applied; delivered alongside Modules 4-5.

modules.title: Test Equipment I: Digital Multimeter & Bench Power Supply
objectives: Measure voltage, current, resistance and continuity safely and accurately
Select ranges/jacks correctly and explain meter CAT ratings
Set voltage and current limits on a bench supply
topics: DMM functions, input impedance, loading, CAT ratings
Current measurement in series; blown-fuse prevention
Bench supply CV/CC modes, current limiting
labs: Measure a resistor kit and compare with color code
Series current measurement on a breadboard
Current-limit a supply to protect a load
modules.assessment: Practical check-off: 10 measurements within tolerance, no unsafe meter use
modules.notes: Hands-on emphasis for new techs; Nida, CIE, USAF and Army all teach the meter early.

modules.title: DC Fundamentals: Ohm's Law, Power, Series & Parallel
objectives: Explain voltage, current, resistance and power
Apply Ohm's law and the power law
Analyze series, parallel and series-parallel circuits
topics: Ohm's law, power, energy, resistor wattage ratings
Opens, shorts and their measured symptoms
labs: Build & measure series, parallel and combination circuits; compare predicted vs. measured
Overpower a resistor (controlled) to show derating
modules.assessment: Written test (80%) + lab notebook review

modules.title: DC Circuit Analysis: Kirchhoff's Laws & Dividers
objectives: Apply KVL and KCL
Design and verify voltage and current dividers
Explain loading and (intro) Thevenin equivalents
modules.assessment: Written test (80%); practical: predict and verify 3 node voltages
modules.notes: MIT 6.002 / AAS depth trimmed to technician level.

modules.title: Components & Data Sheets
objectives: Identify common passive and electromechanical parts by sight and marking
Read resistor/capacitor codes and polarity markings
Extract key ratings from a data sheet
topics: Resistors (types, color/SMD codes), capacitors (types, polarity, voltage rating), inductors
Part numbers, reference designators, data-sheet ratings
labs: Relay coil & contact test with DMM
modules.assessment: Practical ID quiz (90%) + data-sheet scavenger hunt
modules.notes: Feeds directly into soldering and assembly work.

modules.title: Test Equipment II & AC Fundamentals: Oscilloscope & Function Generator
objectives: Describe sine, square and pulse waveforms (peak, p-p, RMS, frequency, period, duty cycle)
Operate an oscilloscope (vertical, horizontal, trigger, probe compensation, grounding)
Use a function generator to drive circuits
topics: Oscilloscope controls, 10x probes, ground-lead hazards, cursors/automatic measurements
labs: Measure generator signals and compare with DMM AC readings
modules.assessment: Practical scope check-off (set up and measure 5 signals unaided) + quiz (80%)
modules.notes: Scope & generator listed by USAF EPI, Army 94F, CIE, Nida, CETa.

modules.title: Reactive Circuits: Capacitors, Inductors, RC/RL/RLC & Transformers
objectives: Explain capacitive/inductive reactance and impedance
Measure RC time constants and filter response
Explain transformer turns ratio and isolation
modules.assessment: Written test (75%) + lab report

modules.title: Semiconductors: Diodes, LEDs, Transistors as Switches
objectives: Test diodes and transistors with a DMM
Explain rectification and Zener regulation
Use BJT and MOSFET as switches to drive loads
topics: BJT & MOSFET basics, switching a relay/LED, flyback diodes
labs: Build a bridge rectifier & view ripple on scope
modules.assessment: Written test (80%) + practical component test

modules.title: Power Supplies & Regulation
objectives: Trace a linear supply block-by-block (transformer, rectifier, filter, regulator)
Measure ripple and load regulation
Recognize switching-supply hazards
labs: Build a regulated 5 V supply; measure ripple and regulation under load
modules.assessment: Practical: supply meets spec; short quiz

modules.title: Amplifier & Op-Amp Basics
objectives: Explain gain, input/output, clipping
Build inverting/non-inverting op-amp circuits and a comparator
modules.assessment: Quiz (75%) + lab verification
modules.notes: Kept brief for entry level; deeper analog is optional.

modules.title: Digital Fundamentals
objectives: Use binary/hex and Boolean logic
Identify gates, flip-flops and counters on schematics
Probe logic levels with a DMM, logic probe and scope
topics: Logic gates, truth tables, logic families & levels (TTL/CMOS)
modules.assessment: Written test (80%) + practical

modules.title: Schematics, Drawings & Technical Documentation
objectives: Read schematic symbols, reference designators and net labels
Correlate schematic, assembly drawing and physical board
Follow work instructions, travelers and revision control
topics: Assembly drawings, BOMs, pin numbering, connector pinouts
labs: Trace a real board against its schematic
Build a small circuit from a schematic only
Mark up a wiring diagram for a harness
modules.assessment: Practical: locate 10 items on board from schematic; quiz
modules.notes: Mirrors USAF 'technical data' and Army technical-manual tasks.

modules.title: Hand Soldering I: Through-Hole & Wires/Terminals
objectives: Explain solder/flux chemistry, wetting, and intermetallics
Make acceptable through-hole and terminal joints
Desolder without pad/trace damage
topics: Tools: iron/tip selection, temperature, fume extraction
Solder alloys (SnPb vs. lead-free), flux, cleaning
Lead forming, hole fill, wire stripping & tinning, turret/cup/hook terminals
modules.assessment: Workmanship inspection of practice board to IPC criteria (target Class 3 with defect log) + written quiz
modules.notes: Aerospace: IPC J-STD-001 (Space Addendum for flight hardware); NASA-STD-8739.3 is superseded by J-STD-001xS.

modules.title: Hand Soldering II: SMT & Rework
objectives: Place and solder chip, SOIC/gull-wing and fine-pitch parts
Use hot air and magnification correctly
Identify common SMT defects
topics: Hot-air rework, solder wick, flux use
labs: SMT practice board (0805 -> SOIC -> fine pitch)
Remove/replace an SOIC with hot air
modules.assessment: Workmanship inspection to IPC-A-610 criteria + practical demonstration

modules.title: Workmanship Inspection & Quality Standards
objectives: Explain IPC product classes 1/2/3 and target/acceptable/defect
Inspect assemblies and record defects
Understand the role of standards in aerospace hardware
topics: IPC-A-610 and J-STD-001 structure, order of precedence
Common defects (cold joint, bridging, insufficient wetting, damage)
labs: Inspect a deliberately-defected board and complete a defect log
modules.assessment: Inspection exercise: find >=90% of seeded defects
modules.notes: Prepares techs for formal IPC CIS certification (optional module).

modules.title: Wiring, Crimping, Cable & Harness Fundamentals
objectives: Select wire gauge/insulation and strip without nicks
Make and inspect crimped contacts with calibrated tools
Build, lace/tie, label and continuity/insulation test a small harness
topics: Crimp tools, die selection, pull-test concept, crimp inspection
labs: Build a multi-branch harness from a drawing
modules.assessment: Harness inspection against A-620 criteria + written quiz

modules.title: Systematic Troubleshooting
objectives: Apply a structured method (symptom -> half-split -> verify -> repair -> retest)
Use meter and scope together to isolate faults to a component
Document findings clearly
topics: Troubleshooting models (half-splitting, signal tracing, input/output checks)
Common failure modes (opens, shorts, drifted parts, cold joints, connectors)
modules.assessment: Practical: isolate 3 of 4 unknown faults within time limit; troubleshooting report
modules.notes: Central to Navy ETN, USAF, Army 94F, CIE and Nida.

modules.title: Capstone: Build, Inspect, Test & Troubleshoot
objectives: Build a small assembly + harness from documentation
Inspect, test and correct it
Present results
labs: Kit build (e.g., regulated supply + digital counter + interface harness) to drawings and workmanship standard
modules.assessment: Capstone rubric: workmanship, functional test, documentation, troubleshooting debrief

optional.title: Microcontrollers & Embedded Basics
optional.content: Microcontroller architecture, GPIO, serial buses (UART/I2C/SPI), flashing firmware, using a logic analyzer.
optional.drawnFrom: Navy ETN, NEETS, Greenville, Nida, CETa (interfacing)

optional.title: RF & Communications Fundamentals
optional.content: Frequency/wavelength, transmission lines, coax & connectors, impedance matching, antennas, RF safety (MPE), spectrum analyzer and VNA basics.

optional.title: Power Electronics & Motors
optional.content: Switching regulators, MOSFET drivers, DC/stepper/BLDC motors, relays/contactors, high-voltage safety.
optional.drawnFrom: NEETS, Navy ETN, USAF EP, Greenville, Nida

optional.title: Instrumentation, Sensors & Data Acquisition
optional.content: Transducers (temperature, pressure, strain), signal conditioning, ADC/DAC, calibration and metrology.
optional.drawnFrom: Navy ETN I&C, N. Seattle metrology, Nida transducers

optional.title: Fiber Optic Terminations
optional.content: Fiber types, safety, termination, inspection, loss testing.

optional.title: Advanced Analog & Circuit Analysis
optional.content: Small-signal transistor amplifiers, Thevenin/Norton, filters, second-order transients.

optional.title: Formal IPC / NASA Certification (CIS)
optional.content: Instructor-led J-STD-001 (Space Addendum), IPC-A-610, IPC/WHMA-A-620 or NASA-STD-8739.4 certification through an authorized training center.
